who.value: buyer looking for a home-service provider

job.value: Compare suggested service providers and pick which to ask for a quote

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: Provider cards with ratings, tags and 'Select for quote', under '3+ providers in Singapore', read as a list of providers to choose from.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: 'Select for quote' repeats on every card but is a small black text link, no stronger than the tags above it.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Select for quote' and 'Certified' / 'All' tabs are clear, but the grey photo tiles beside each provider have no hint whether they open the provider or listings.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: Tags like 'HDB/Condo', '24/7' and 'Licensed' are familiar locally, but 'Preferred' in a red badge isn't explained.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: Choosing which providers to ask for a quote is something the person can do from ratings and tags.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Each card shows only rating, review count and 2–3 tags; detail is behind the provider.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: The search bar, tabs and provider list all serve finding a provider.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: Names, star ratings and short tags carry the cards; there's no explanatory text.
